subject.title: OpenAI Codex OAuth can bind to a deactivated ChatGPT workspace when accounts have multiple workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw automatically recover from a deactivated ChatGPT workspace for multi-workspace OpenAI/Codex OAuth accounts, and at which boundary should that recovery persist the active accountId?
rationale: The remaining fix changes auth-profile semantics, provider routing, and fallback/remediation behavior; the source shows several viable owners, but code alone cannot choose whether OpenClaw should auto-select, retry, persist, or only guide reauthentication.

options.title: OpenAI plugin owns recovery
options.body: Validate or recover a usable ChatGPT accountId after OAuth and on `deactivated_workspace`, then persist the recovered id for provider and app-server use.

options.title: Remediation only
options.body: Keep the classifier mitigation and add clearer in-product guidance or doctor/onboarding recovery without automatically changing stored workspace selection.

options.title: Use explicit workspace selection
options.body: Expose or derive an explicit upstream-compatible workspace selection contract, then enforce it instead of guessing among available workspaces.

recommendation.title: OpenAI plugin owns recovery
recommendation.body: Validate or recover a usable ChatGPT accountId after OAuth and on `deactivated_workspace`, then persist the recovered id for provider and app-server use.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the Codex OAuth ownership and auth-bridge refactor history from #68284.
